original_question: Suppose n >= 2 and Lambda is a lattice in R^(n+1) with positive homogeneous minimum N(Lambda) > 0, where N(Lambda) is the infimum of |z_0 z_1 ... z_n| over nonzero lattice points z = (z_0, ..., z_n). Must every such lattice be algebraic?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in §1, subsection "Lattices with positive minima".
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core mathematical target very well: it has the right ambient dimension parameter n >= 2, the right object (a lattice in R^(n+1)), the right positivity hypothesis on the multiplicative/homogeneous minimum N(Lambda), the correct formula for N(Lambda) as an infimum of coordinate products over nonzero lattice points, and the right yes/no issue—whether such lattices must be algebraic.
missing_details: The paper’s notion of an algebraic lattice is not implicit; it comes from a totally real algebraic number field K of degree n+1 and a full Z-module in K, embedded into R^(n+1) via the n+1 real embeddings of K.
The question should make clear that Lambda is a full lattice of rank n+1 in R^(n+1), not an arbitrary discrete subgroup of smaller rank.
The paper’s nearby setup explains algebraicity through the standard Minkowski-type embedding of a full module in a totally real field; without this, the word "algebraic" is underspecified.
The paper’s context is specifically real/totally real because the target space is R^(n+1); your draft does not state that restriction.
It is helpful to state the universal quantifiers explicitly: for every integer n >= 2 and every full lattice Lambda in R^(n+1) with N(Lambda) > 0.
The nearby context ties the conjecture to multiplicative Diophantine approximation through a special lattice construction in Proposition 1.2; your draft omits that motivating specialization.

The paper’s terminology is closer to a multiplicative minimum/positive minimum of a lattice; your draft uses "homogeneous minimum," which is mathematically understandable but not fully paper-faithful unless the exact paper terminology is restored.
refined_question: For every integer n >= 2, let Lambda be a full lattice in R^(n+1), and define its multiplicative minimum by N(Lambda) = inf{|x_1 x_2 ... x_(n+1)| : x = (x_1, ..., x_(n+1)) in Lambda \ {0}}. If N(Lambda) > 0, must Lambda be an algebraic lattice in the paper’s sense—namely, a lattice arising from a full Z-module in a totally real algebraic number field K of degree n+1 under the embedding of K into R^(n+1) given by its n+1 real embeddings?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s subsection on lattices with positive minima. In that subsection, the author first recalls the standard construction of lattices coming from a totally real algebraic field and notes that such lattices have positive multiplicative minimum; he then states Conjecture 1.1 asking whether the converse holds. Proposition 1.2 gives the special Diophantine-approximation reformulation for lattices attached to a vector (theta_1, ..., theta_n), and Theorem 1.3 explains why this conjectural converse would have consequences for Littlewood-type problems. So the nearest official target is exactly Conjecture 1.1, not a broader neighboring problem.
